findings.reason: All three original standalone tiles show only prose. A digon with two distinct corners, opposed boundary traversal and an auxiliary splitting diameter concretely clarifies the vertex classes and the passage from one face to two disks glued along their whole boundaries. A hemisphere schematic then explains where those glued boundaries go; this is warranted exposition despite the complete independent proof.

diagram_math_checks.data: D has corners v0 at left and v1 at right; upper side s1:a is traversed left-to-right, lower s2:a^{-1} right-to-left.
diagram_math_checks.check: The arrows represent the Given parameter directions. Reversal s1(t)~s2(1-t) fixes both corners separately: t=0 pairs v0 with v0 and t=1 pairs v1 with v1 (Verification 1.1). They are explicitly not reference-direction arrows. No extra corner identifications or twisted pair is drawn.

diagram_math_checks.data: Dashed gamma joins the corners through the interior; B1 above, B2 below.
diagram_math_checks.check: These are the two bigons of Verification 1.2: partial B1=s1 union gamma, partial B2=s2 union gamma-prime after cutting. The caption specifies regluing the two copies and combining this with the side pairing into h:partial B1->partial B2. It explicitly excludes counting gamma as an edge of the original CW structure, which still has V=2,E=1,F=1. Supplier reduction lemma 1.1 permits round representatives, and 1.2 supplies the split quotient identity.

diagram_math_checks.data: q:D->Y and Phi:Y->S2; figure arrow Phi composed with q:D->S2.
diagram_math_checks.check: q is the quotient map from the Given quotient. Phi is the homeomorphism constructed in Verification 2.1, with the source identified via the split in 1.2. The composite has the shown disk domain and sphere codomain; only Y congruent S2 is asserted, not D congruent S2.

diagram_math_checks.data: Right circle depicts sphere, central ellipse equator, upper/lower regions labelled S2_+, S2_-.
diagram_math_checks.check: Verification 2.1 maps B1 to the upper closed hemisphere via the positive square root and B2 to the lower via the negative square root. On each boundary the disk coordinate has norm one, so t=0; alpha2 composed with h=alpha1 ensures agreement and both boundary images are exactly the equator. Thus Phi(partial B1)=Phi(partial B2) means images of their quotient classes, as in the proof. This is schematic perspective, not a planar embedding claim.
